phase: research8 phase 1: stock return distribution models
purpose: Forecast the full distribution of a stock's log total return from a close to 1-63 sessions later, using stock history and the earnings calendar only (no option quotes). Phase 2 turns the frozen distribution(s) into option values. This phase is scored by forecast accuracy only; it makes no trading claim.

user_decisions.split: names x time: develop on the original 300 names through 2022; untouched test on the 500 expanded names from 2023 (user choice, 2026-10-03)
user_decisions.scores: try many: report every score below for every model; freeze the dev winner of each primary score (user choice)
user_decisions.release_dates: an upcoming release date is known when it is at most 30 calendar days after the forecast date; otherwise it is projected (user choice)

data.stocks: OptionMetrics daily open/high/low/close/return/cfadj from research7-data-2026-10 (original 300) and research7-expanded-2026-10 (expanded 500), 2014-01-02 to 2025-08-29
data.events: I/B/E/S quarterly EPS announcement date and time from the same releases (events_original/events_expanded), 2014 onward

returns.daily: r_t = log(1 + return_t), OptionMetrics total return (split-adjusted, dividends included)
returns.intraday: id_t = log(|close_t| / open_t) when open, high, low > 0; else missing
returns.overnight: on_t = r_t - id_t (contains dividends and any overnight news)
returns.range_variance: gk_t = 0.5 log(high_t/low_t)^2 - (2 log 2 - 1) id_t^2 (Garman-Klass intraday variance), missing when id_t is
returns.target: R_{t,h} = sum of r over the h sessions after the origin close t; requires every one of those returns to exist

release_days.rule: Release timing as research7: before open -> release return is the session of the announcement date; after close -> the next session; non-session announcement date -> the first session after it; during the session -> the announcement-date session. One release per security and fiscal period end (earliest announcement).
release_days.release_return: J = r on the release session (close P to close Q)
release_days.diffusion_days: every other session; release-session returns are excluded from all diffusion estimates and diffusion targets
release_days.known_at_origin: For origin t, the next release is used at its actual session if its announcement date is <= t + 30 calendar days. Otherwise the release is projected at the first session on or after (last known announcement date + 91 calendar days), repeated as needed. If no earlier release exists, none is projected.
release_days.in_window: A forecast for horizon h includes a jump component for each known or projected release session inside (t, t+h].

samples.dev: original-group names; origins whose target session is <= 2022-12-30; first origin 2016-01-04
samples.test: expanded_2017 and added_2020 names; origins >= 2023-01-03 with a complete target (data end 2025-08-29). Untouched: no score of any kind has been computed on it before freezing.
samples.secondary_after_freeze: Reported only after freezing, never used to choose: original names with origins >= 2023-01-03 (time holdout) and expanded names with targets <= 2022-12-30 (name holdout).
samples.origins: Every fifth session counted from 2014-01-02 (a fixed weekly grid), plus every release forecast below. Eligible when the origin close is >= $5 and the name has >= 252 earlier sessions with returns.
samples.release_forecasts: For every release with a known P close: a 1-session forecast from the P close of the release return J (scored separately as 'release day').

estimation.walk_forward: Pooled parameters are re-estimated at each 1 January from data dated before it whose targets are realized before it; forecasts during that year use those parameters plus each name's data up to the origin close.
estimation.test_training_names: all 800 names (data before each refit date)

diffusion_variance.EWMA: Daily variance on diffusion days: seed with the mean of the first 20 squared returns, then var = 0.94 var + 0.06 r^2 (release returns skipped). Horizon variance = n_d x var, n_d = diffusion sessions in the window.
diffusion_variance.GARCH: GJR-GARCH(1,1) on diffusion days, var_{t+1} = w + (a + g 1[r_t<0]) r_t^2 + b var_t, with variance targeting w = (1 - a - g/2 - b) LR where LR is the name's mean squared diffusion return over its last 504 sessions. a, g, b and the Student-t df are pooled across training names (quasi-ML). Horizon variance sums the multi-step forecasts LR + p^(k-1)(var_{t+1} - LR), p = a + g/2 + b, over diffusion sessions.
diffusion_variance.HAR: Per horizon h, pooled least squares of log(mean future diffusion proxy) on logs of overnight-squared means over 5/22/66 sessions and Garman-Klass means over 1/5/22/66 sessions, where the daily proxy is on_t^2 + gk_t. Forecast daily variance = exp(fit) x mean(exp(residual)) (smearing), horizon variance = n_d x that.

shape.calibration: Every shape is fitted to standardized diffusion returns z = D_{t,h} / sqrt(horizon variance) from training data, per horizon, where D is the target minus any release returns inside the window. This also corrects any scale bias of the variance model.
shape.Gauss: Normal with the training standard deviation of z
shape.T: Student-t fitted to z by maximum likelihood (df, location 0, scale)
shape.FHS: Empirical quantiles of the training z (filtered historical simulation), with pooled z from the most recent 5 years of training data

jump.none: No separate release component (releases treated as ordinary days; note the diffusion variance still excludes release returns, so 'none' measures the cost of ignoring the calendar)
jump.name: J drawn uniformly from the name's last 8 release returns (need >= 4); with fewer, use 'shrunk'
jump.shrunk: J = s_J x u, where s_J^2 = (n m + k0 c v) / (n + k0): n = number of the name's last 8 release returns, m = their mean square, v = the diffusion daily variance at the origin, c = pooled training mean of J^2 / v at P, k0 = 4; u drawn from the pooled training standardized jumps J / s_J (with s_J computed as of each P).

components.combination: For each forecast the distribution of D + sum of jumps is formed from 4,000 stratified diffusion draws paired with randomly ordered jump draws (fixed seed); quantiles are read from the combined draws. Without a jump the shape quantiles are scaled directly.

candidates.B0_EWMA_raw_Gauss: Baseline: EWMA 0.94 on all returns including releases, Normal with variance h x var, no calibration and no calendar
candidates.B1_HS_name: Baseline: empirical quantiles of the name's own overlapping h-session returns over the last 504 sessions (unfiltered historical simulation)
candidates.grid: diffusion {EWMA, GARCH, HAR} x shape {Gauss, T, FHS} x jump {none, name, shrunk} = 27 models
candidates.GBQ: Gradient-boosted quantiles: sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor (loss=quantile, max_iter 300, learning_rate 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 31, min_samples_leaf 200, seed 0) per horizon and level 0.01/0.05/0.10/0.25/0.50/0.75/0.90/0.95/0.99, fitted on weekly-grid training origins to y = R_{t,h} / sqrt(h x EWMA var). Features: log EWMA var; log 5/22/66-session means of on^2 and gk; log 252-session mean squared diffusion return; 22- and 66-session returns divided by EWMA vol; known/projected release in window (0/1); sessions to that release / h; log(s_J^2 / v) from 'shrunk'; n of name release history; log close. Predicted quantiles are sorted, then interpolated linearly in standard-normal score with linear tail extension to the full grid.

scores.CRPS: Quantile-score approximation: CRPS = 2 x trapezoid integral over the level grid of the pinball loss. Reported as skill 1 - mean(model)/mean(B0) per horizon.
scores.twCRPS: Same with level weight (2 tau - 1)^2 (tail-weighted, Gneiting-Ranjan)
scores.log_score: Log density at the outcome from a piecewise-linear CDF through the quantiles, with exponential tails beyond 0.001/0.999 matching the outer interval's density; reported as mean difference from B0 (nats)
scores.PIT: Interpolated CDF value at the outcome; reported as coverage of central 50/80/90/98% intervals and the maximum absolute deviation of the PIT histogram (20 bins) from uniform
scores.abs_move: Predicted E|R| (mean of |quantile| over a uniform level sub-grid) against realized |R|: ratio of means realized/predicted and mean squared error of |R| (what an ATM straddle pays)
scores.inference: Differences from B0 and from the dev-best model: means with 95% intervals from a bootstrap over calendar weeks of the origin (2,000 draws, seed 20261003).

freeze_rule: On dev, freeze at most four distinct models: the best mean CRPS skill averaged over the seven horizons; the best mean log-score difference averaged over the seven horizons; the best mean twCRPS skill averaged over the seven horizons; and the best release-day CRPS. Ties keep the simpler model (fewer components, grid before GBQ). Frozen specs, with every dev score, are committed before the test data are scored.
test_gates: A frozen model passes for its own score if on test (1) its improvement over B0 on that score has a weekly-bootstrap 95% lower bound above zero, (2) it also improves on B0 in CRPS at every horizon group, and (3) central 90% interval coverage is within 0.85-0.95 at every horizon. All 31 models are reported on test as diagnostics; only frozen ones can pass.
outputs: Aggregate tables only in docs/research8/phase1 (public). Per-forecast scores stay in a private directory; their SHA-256 values are recorded.
known_limitations: I/B/E/S announcement times are retrospective, not a point-in-time calendar.
Quarter-ahead release dates beyond 30 days are projected crudely (+91 days).
Dev names overlap the names used by research4-7 option studies; their stock-distribution forecasts were never scored there.
Close-to-close horizons only; intraday option exits are not modelled in this phase.
